solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Arab lord at sea finds the coast

indicators.note: being at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters of the two words before are jumbled

explanation.surface: An Arab nobleman out sailing catches sight of land.
explanation.definitionFit: Labrador is the long Atlantic seaboard of mainland Newfoundland and Labrador in Canada, a coast in its own right.

clue.text: Born with attractive feature, Fred stripped!

definitions.note: Fred appearing in a comic strip, read as a playful description

parts.note: B is the usual abbreviation for born, as in family trees
an asset is a quality that counts in someone's favour

explanation.surface: Someone named Fred, good-looking from birth, has taken his clothes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stripped' suggests undressing, but here it means appearing in a strip cartoon: Fred Basset is a dog in a long-running British newspaper comic strip.
explanation.definitionFit: Fred Basset is the hound star of a Daily Mail comic strip, so the strip's Fred is a basset.

clue.text: Brute Hitler, losing head, wrote in frenzy

indicators.note: writing in a frenzy suggests wild disorder, so the letters are scrambled
the dictator's name loses its first letter, its head

explanation.surface: A historical tyrant is pictured beheaded and scribbling madly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' drops H from HITLER to leave ITLER; 'in frenzy' then mixes ITLER with WROTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rottweiler is a powerful, aggressive guard dog, so it can fairly be called a brute.

clue.text: Compares to Sheridan's play article ignored

indicators.note: the article is ignored, meaning left out of the play's title

parts.note: A 1775 comedy by Richard Brinsley Sheridan
the definite article is THE

explanation.surface: A critic compares something to a Sheridan play while overlooking an article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored' removes THE from the title THE RIVALS.
explanation.definitionFit: To rival something is to match or equal it, so the verb works as 'compares to' in the sense of stands comparison with.

clue.text: Wanted no change having bought Irishman drink?

parts.note: to stand someone a drink is to buy it for them, so bought (a drink) gives this verb
Pat, short for Patrick, is the stock crossword name for an Irishman

explanation.surface: Someone who paid for an Irishman's drink declined the change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanted no change' looks like turning down coins at the bar; it really means refusing to alter a position, as a poker player holding his cards does.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand pat is an idiom from poker for keeping one's hand, hence refusing any change of course.

clue.text: Greek character with Tees an ignoramus!

parts.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet
two letter T's, as the plural of the letter tee

explanation.surface: A Greek person, together with the setter Tees, is a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: Tees is this setter's own name, but here it simply means two Ts.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutt is slang for a stupid or incompetent person, a dimwit or blockhead.

clue.text: Crazy compilers surmount decent chap in lawless place

indicators.note: in a down entry the first pieces sit on top of the saint

parts.note: wild can mean crazy or frenzied
setters often refer to themselves in the plural as we
ST, saint, a thoroughly good person

explanation.surface: Mad crossword setters climb over a nice man in somewhere without laws.
explanation.definitionFit: The American frontier of the nineteenth century is the byword for an area where order and sheriffs barely reached.

clue.text: Spy using Blackbird?

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an eagle is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: A spy flies the Blackbird, the American reconnaissance plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blackbird' must be split into Black and bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Beagle is an old word for a spy or informer, from the dog's tracking nose.

clue.text: Six-footer gathering smallest amount is physician

indicators.note: the insect gathers in, meaning holds within it, the other pieces

parts.note: an insect has six legs, and an ant is an insect
an atom is the tiniest possible quantity
kept as written

explanation.surface: A six-foot doctor picks up the slightest thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' is an insect, not a tall person.
explanation.definitionFit: Physician is used in its old general sense of a scientist of the body; an anatomist studies bodily structure.

clue.text: Make one college tenure vacant?

parts.note: uni is short for university, a seat of higher education

indicators.note: emptied of its inside, so only the outer letters of tenure remain

explanation.surface: A college makes one of its academic tenured posts vacant.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite is to join separate things into a single whole.

clue.text: Clear others holding MDMA

indicators.note: the others hold the drug inside

parts.note: the rest means the others
the drug MDMA is ecstasy, known as E

explanation.surface: Other people are cleared despite carrying ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: To reset a counter or device is to clear it back to zero.

clue.text: See 22
The river through the underworld takes no definite course

indicators.note: the river runs through, meaning inside, the underworld

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and also his realm
kept as written

explanation.surface: A river running through Hades meanders aimlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: Dis is the classical name for the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dithers wavers indecisively, never settling on a line of action.

clue.text: Succeed? Anything but where pence decline in value

parts.note: prices recede when they fall back

explanation.surface: Is there success where the penny loses its value? Far from it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the opposite of succeed: to come before rather than after.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed is to follow on after something; its opposite is to go before.

clue.text: Two males celibate — might be significant

indicators.note: the letters might be rearranged into something else

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male, so two of them are MM

explanation.surface: Two unmarried men who abstain might be a meaningful sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Something emblematic serves as a symbol, so it is significant in the sense of signifying.

clue.text: Line up with chain wheel

parts.note: a row is a line of things
an el is an American elevated railway, a line running up above the street

explanation.surface: Someone lines up a chain with a bicycle sprocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' stands for EL, the US elevated railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowel is the small spiked revolving disc on a rider's spur, a wheel with a chain of points.

clue.text: 12 fully in shot was broadcast

indicators.note: shot means ruined or wrecked, so the letters are broken up

parts.note: the number twelve written out in full

explanation.surface: Twelve, filmed completely in one take, went out on air.
explanation.walkthrough: '12' here is the number, not the cross-reference it seems; 'shot' mixes TWELVE with IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme that went live was transmitted as it happened.

clue.text: Paunch good for Goering

definitions.meaning: the German word for good, as Hermann Goering would say it

explanation.surface: A pot belly is good for Goering, who was notoriously fat.
explanation.definitionFit: A gut is a protruding belly, and the German for good is spelt the same way.

clue.text: Deceiver into girl departs dance

indicators.note: the deceiver goes into the other pieces

parts.note: gal is informal for girl
D is the abbreviation for departs in timetables
a liar deceives

explanation.surface: A con man gets into a relationship with a girl, and she leaves the dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The galliard is a lively Renaissance court dance in triple time.

clue.text: Coarse woman hankering after bachelor

indicators.note: the longing comes after the bachelor

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in degrees
an itch is a restless longing

explanation.surface: A rough woman is longing for a single man.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an insult for an unpleasant, spiteful woman; it also means a female dog, matching the canine theme.

clue.text: Transport to hell worker caught by cunning schemes

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
art in its sense of trickery and wiles

explanation.surface: A worker is ensnared by devious plots on the way to damnation.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the idiom 'going to hell in a handcart', for something rapidly deteriorating.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a hand-pushed cart as the vehicle in which things go to hell.

clue.text: Maiden, single, left to bed Greek bastard

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: one bedding the Greek means holding it inside

parts.note: one is a single unit

explanation.surface: An unmarried girl leaves to sleep with a Greek scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A mongrel is a dog of mixed breed, and both words carry the sense of illegitimate origin.

clue.text: With it sailors follow procedure

indicators.note: the sailors follow, coming after the procedure

parts.note: a mode is a way of doing things
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Sailors go along with standard procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: Being with it means fashionable and current, which is what up-to-date things are.

clue.text: Conduct private business re 1, 2, 3, 6, 8, 19, 21A,24, 27 or 28?

definitions.meaning: a euphemism for slipping away on an undisclosed errand, often a trip to the toilet
all the listed answers are kinds of dog, so a meeting concerning any of them is literally a dog meeting

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a jocular excuse for leaving without saying why, and taken literally it means consulting someone over a hound.

clue.text: Some chosen at Ephesus for worthy body

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people were selected at the ancient city of Ephesus for an honourable council.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft definition included 'for'; that word only links wordplay to definition, so the definition is 'worthy body'.
explanation.definitionFit: A senate is a governing council, traditionally of elders, a body of worthies.

clue.text: After word from Camus, this writer has purpose

indicators.note: the setter's contraction comes after the French word

parts.note: mot is French for word, and Camus wrote in French
the setter saying I have, contracted

explanation.surface: After a remark by Albert Camus, the writer finds meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: IVE is I've, the setter speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A motive is the reason driving an action, its aim or intent.

clue.text: Split personality failing to shine in Chinese city?

indicators.note: the dull finish goes in the city's name

parts.note: Dalian is a port city in north-east China
mat or matt describes a dull, non-glossy finish

explanation.surface: A psychological case of a divided self loses its sparkle in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split personality' is not the disorder: Split is a city in Croatia's Dalmatia region.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Split is a native of Dalmatia; the answer is also the spotted dog breed of the theme.

clue.text: Expert flyer to trap rook and land

indicators.note: the pilot traps the rook inside

parts.note: an ace is a top fighter pilot
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A skilled pilot sets out to snare a bird and then touch down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'land' looks like a verb tied to the flyer; it is the noun, an area of ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land area, and acres can mean land in general.

clue.text: Clown sees hour is time lost to evil figure

indicators.note: these pieces are lost, meaning dropped from the evil figure's name

parts.note: the Antichrist is the great enemy of Christ in Christian tradition
kept as written

explanation.surface: A clown watches an hour slip away to a devilish figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Antic is an old noun for a grotesque performer or buffoon.

clue.text: Lunar vehicle runs past

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
over means finished or past

explanation.surface: A moon buggy speeds by.
explanation.definitionFit: The lunar rover was the buggy driven by Apollo astronauts on the moon; the word is also a dog's name.

clue.text: Retired old robber one saves

parts.note: a riever or reiver is a raider, a word from the old Border lands

explanation.surface: A retired former thief now rescues people.
explanation.walkthrough: Rievers were cattle raiders on the old Anglo-Scottish border.
explanation.definitionFit: A retriever is someone or something that recovers or rescues things, as the gundog brings back game.
